prep.what: Build a durable, persistent background job queue that survives process restarts — the backbone the sweeper (t21) and CI lane (t22) will run on.
prep.understand: Durability means jobs are written to storage (DB or Redis) before being dispatched, so a crash loses nothing. Core flow: enqueue to atomic claim to execute to ack/fail to retry with backoff to dead-letter after max attempts. The key primitive is SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (Postgres) or BLPOP/LMOVE (Redis) for atomic, race-free claiming.
approach: Design the jobs table schema: id, type, payload, status (pending/running/done/failed), attempts, next_retry_at.
Implement enqueue(type, payload) and dequeue() — atomic claim so two workers never grab the same job.
Add retry logic: on failure increment attempts, set next_retry_at with exponential backoff; after max_attempts move to dead-letter.
Write a minimal worker poll loop and tests covering: enqueue to process to done, and failure to retry to dead-letter.
resources: SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (Postgres docs) or BLPOP / LMOVE (Redis command reference)
Search for job, queue, worker, dispatch in the existing codebase for prior patterns
DB migration tooling already in this project

tasks.title: Sweeper
tasks.notes: Depends on durable job queue (t20) — build that first, then this.

prep.what: Implement the sweeper — a scheduled process that cleans up jobs stuck in running state, expired daemon locks, and dead-letter entries.
prep.understand: The sweeper runs on top of the queue you built this morning (t20). It handles failure cases the happy path misses: a worker that crashed mid-job without acking, a lock held by a dead daemon process, jobs past max retries. Key requirement: sweeps must be idempotent — safe to run concurrently with workers.
approach: Define sweep rules: stuck = status=running AND updated_at older than N minutes; expired locks = heartbeat older than lease duration; reap = status=failed AND attempts >= max_attempts.
Implement each rule as a named, logged operation — makes debugging easy when something gets incorrectly reaped.
Wire the sweeper into the scheduler: either as a recurring job type on the queue itself, or a separate cron-triggered process.
Test: seed a stuck job, run sweeper, assert it is re-queued; seed a dead-letter entry, run reaper, assert it is archived.
